questions.question: Explain why a labour-abundant country specializes in labour-intensive goods according to the Heckscher–Ohlin Theory. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why labour – abundant country specializes in labour – intensive goods
  • according to Heckscher Ohlin Theory.
  • • Labour abundance: The country has more labour relative to capital.
  • • Lower labour cost: Abundant labour makes labour relatively cheaper.
  • • Labour-intensive goods: These goods require more labour than capital.
  • • Comparative advantage: Such goods can be produced at a lower relative cost.
  • • Specialization: The country specializes in and exports labour-intensive goods.
  • • Example: India exports garments and textiles due to its large labour force.

questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of bank rate policy in correcting BoP disequilibrium.
  • • Higher bank rate: Reduces borrowing and money supply.
  • • Lower imports: Reduces spending and demand for imported goods.
  • • Foreign capital inflow: Higher interest rates may attract foreign investment.
  • • Controls inflation: May improve export competitiveness.
  • • Corrects BoP deficit: Reduces foreign exchange outflow and encourages inflow.

questions.question: Explain, with the help of a suitable diagram, how the equilibrium exchange rate is determined in the foreign exchange market. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain with help of diagram, how equilibrium exchange rate is determined in foreign
  • exchange market.
  • • Demand for foreign exchange (D): Slopes downward.
  • • Supply of foreign exchange (S): Slopes upward.
  • • Equilibrium exchange rate: D=S
  • • Equilibrium point (E): Intersection of demand and supply curves.
  • • Above equilibrium: Excess supply of foreign exchange.
  • • Below equilibrium: Excess demand for foreign exchange.
